microarchitecture_summary.implementation_style: Single-module synthesizable RTL with one synchronous clock domain, using internal counters and registers to create a PWM breathing LED effect suitable for FPGA open-source flows.
microarchitecture_summary.control_strategy: A slow counter acts as a clock-enable generator for brightness updates; the 8-bit duty register increments or decrements only on the slow tick, while an internal direction bit reverses at 8'h00 and 8'hFF. The PWM counter free-runs continuously and is compared against the duty register to determine led.
microarchitecture_summary.state_strategy: Internal state consists of a slow divider counter, an 8-bit free-running PWM counter, an 8-bit duty-cycle register, and a single direction bit. Safe deterministic power-up values should be used where supported by the target flow so the design starts in a valid breathing sequence without an external reset.
microarchitecture_summary.output_strategy: Drive led directly from the PWM compare result between the free-running 8-bit PWM counter and the current 8-bit duty-cycle register, active-high at the RTL level.

fsm_intent.description: No explicit multi-state FSM is implied or required. The behavior is realized with simple counter and direction-bit updates on the clock edge.

internal_storage: Slow divider counter used to generate a visible update tick.
8-bit PWM counter that increments every clk cycle.
8-bit duty-cycle register holding the current brightness level.
Direction bit indicating whether the duty cycle is ramping up or down.
output_mapping: led is asserted when the PWM counter is below the duty-cycle register, forming a standard counter-versus-duty PWM waveform.
The slow divider counter produces a periodic step event used to update the duty register and direction bit; it does not create a derived clock.

sequencing_notes: All sequential logic uses clk only; no derived clocks or asynchronous controls are introduced.
The PWM counter advances on every clock cycle.
The duty-cycle register updates only on slow tick events from the divider logic.
On each slow tick, the duty cycle increments when direction is up and decrements when direction is down.
Direction flips when the duty register reaches either endpoint, 8'hFF or 8'h00.
Initialization should be deterministic where supported, but the design must remain synthesizable even if explicit register initialization is not honored by a target.
timing_notes: The slow divider width should be large enough to make the breathing effect visibly slow on a typical demo board clock.
The PWM counter is intended to run at the full board clock rate so the LED waveform flicker is minimized.
The compare path should remain a simple register-versus-counter comparison for easy synthesis and timing closure.
The design is intended for lint, Yosys synthesis, nextpnr place-and-route, and timing review without vendor primitives or special constraints inside RTL.
ownership_notes: The top module pwm_fpga_demo owns all internal state and the complete LED breathing behavior.
Board-specific starter constraints are external to RTL and are generated separately after board selection.
Use PCF for iCE40 boards and LPF for ECP5 boards; constraints are demo bring-up only and require review before hardware programming.
consistency_notes: Interfaces remain exactly as defined in digital_spec_json.
